predecessors.name: Kingdom of Georgia
predecessors.text: Guria on the Black Sea, one of the 'western provinces' George VIII lost after the Battle of Chikhori in 1463

successors.name: Russian Empire
successors.text: Guria, deposed by Russia on 2 September 1829 and made the Ozurgeti uyezd of Kutais Governorate in 1840 (without Adjara, which Russia took from the Ottomans in 1878)

ledger.x: 1463: the Gurieli make Guria independent of the Georgian crown.
1540s: the Ottomans take the south of Guria.
1609: Mamia II Gurieli retakes Adjara from the Ottomans.
13 December 1614: Mamia II renounces Adjara to the Ottomans.
By 1723 the Ottomans hold Batumi and Chakvi and garrison the coast.
1772: Kobuleti is cut from Guria after Guria backs Russia.
1829: Russia deposes Prince David and annexes Guria.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1768-1774)
wars.outcome: Gurian support for Russia prompted an Ottoman reaction and Kobuleti was detached from Guria (Guria page); the Imereti side of the war is in the Imereti dossier.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1806-1812)
wars.outcome: 'On June 19, 1810, Mamia V accepted Russian suzerainty, becoming an autonomous principality' (Guria page).

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1828-1829)
wars.outcome: Princess Sophia of Guria sided with the Turks; Russia deposed Prince David on 2 September 1829 and the Treaty of Adrianople (14 September 1829) had the Sultan recognize Russia's possession of 'Georgia (with Imeretia, Mingrelia, Guria)'.

certainty.note: A small principality between the Ottoman coast and Imereti; no treaty line or survey on the pages.
